new_entities.name: Oral intestinal alkaline phosphatase
new_entities.description: Orally administered intestinal alkaline phosphatase or related exogenous alkaline-phosphatase formulations promoted for gut-barrier and endotoxin-detoxifying effects.

new_entities.name: Endotoxaemia
new_entities.description: Systemic exposure to endotoxin or lipopolysaccharide-related inflammatory burden associated with gut barrier dysfunction.

edges.population: humans or translational models receiving exogenous intestinal alkaline phosphatase to modulate gut-derived inflammation or endotoxin burden
edges.mechanism: Intestinal alkaline phosphatase can dephosphorylate lipopolysaccharide and other microbial ligands, which provides a biologically coherent route for lowering endotoxin signaling and improving gut barrier resilience.
edges.summary: Oral intestinal alkaline phosphatase has one of the clearest mechanistic stories in the whole gut-supplement space, but human evidence remains early and indirect. The literature supports a plausible anti-endotoxin role, yet direct clinical proof that oral supplementation lowers endotoxaemia in humans is still thin.
edges.caveats: Most of the strongest endotoxin evidence is mechanistic or animal-based. The available human trial was in ulcerative colitis and tracked inflammatory activity rather than a clean endotoxemia endpoint.

evidence.citation: LukasM et al 2010 Inflamm Bowel Dis
evidence.notes: Exogenous alkaline phosphatase for the treatment of patients with moderate to severe ulcerative colitis.

evidence.citation: EstakiM et al 2014 World J Gastroenterol
evidence.notes: Interplay between intestinal alkaline phosphatase, diet, gut microbes and immunity.
Role of Intestinal Alkaline Phosphatase in Innate Immunity.
